scenes.heading: Mitosis and meiosis
scenes.sub: How one fertilised egg became all of you
scenes.say: Every cell in your body came from one fertilised egg. Your gametes came from a special division that halves the chromosome number. So how do cells divide, and what controls it?

scenes.heading: Cyclins and checkpoints
points: Cycle: G1, S, G2, then M
CDKs only work when bound to a cyclin
scenes.say: The cell cycle runs G one, S, G two, then M. Cyclins are the seasons and C D Ks are the engine: the engine is always there, but only runs when its cyclin arrives. Checkpoints pause the cycle if something's wrong. p fifty-three spots DNA damage, and R b guards the gate into S phase.
scenes.caption: The cell cycle runs G1, S, G2, then M. Cyclins are the seasons and CDKs are the engine: the engine is always there, but only runs when its cyclin arrives. Checkpoints pause the cycle if something's wrong. p53 spots DNA damage, and Rb guards the gate into S phase.

scenes.heading: Think of it like this
scenes.everyday: A train won't leave until every door is closed
scenes.science: Anaphase won't start until every kinetochore is attached
scenes.breaks: There's no 'all clear' message: each unattached kinetochore sends a 'wait' signal, and anaphase starts when the last one goes quiet.
scenes.say: A train can't leave the station while even one door is open. At the spindle checkpoint, the cell won't start anaphase until every kinetochore is attached to the spindle. One unattached kinetochore keeps the cell waiting, so daughter cells don't get the wrong number of chromosomes.

scenes.heading: Mitosis: PMAT
steps: Metaphase: line up in the Middle
scenes.say: Mitosis is P M A T, with prometaphase after prophase. Chromosomes condense, then the nuclear envelope breaks down. At metaphase they line up in the middle. At anaphase, sister chromatids move away to opposite poles. At telophase, new nuclei form. Result: two identical cells.
scenes.caption: Mitosis is PMAT, with prometaphase after prophase. Chromosomes condense, then the nuclear envelope breaks down. At metaphase they line up in the Middle. At anaphase, sister chromatids move Away to opposite poles. At telophase, new nuclei form. Result: two identical cells.

scenes.heading: Meiosis I vs meiosis II
scenes.say: Meiosis one separates partners: homologous pairs split, so the chromosome number halves. Meiosis two separates twins: sister chromatids split, just like mitosis. The result is four genetically different haploid cells.

scenes.heading: Cross, Shuffle, Meet
points: Cross: crossing over in prophase I
scenes.say: Variation comes from cross, shuffle, meet. Crossing over in prophase one. Independent assortment in metaphase one, like twenty-three light switches: that's about eight point four million combinations. And random fertilisation when gametes meet.
scenes.caption: Variation comes from Cross, Shuffle, Meet. Crossing over in prophase I. Independent assortment in metaphase I, like 23 light switches: 2²³ is about 8.4 million combinations. And random fertilisation when gametes meet.

scenes.heading: Non-disjunction
scenes.question: One pair of homologues fails to separate in meiosis I in a human cell. What are the four gametes?
lines: Both homologues go to one cell
scenes.say: If one pair of homologues fails to separate in meiosis one, both go into one cell. Meiosis two runs normally. You get two gametes with twenty-four chromosomes and two with twenty-two. All four are abnormal. An extra chromosome twenty-one causes Down syndrome.

points: Checkpoints at G1, G2/M and spindle
scenes.say: Quick recap. Cyclins and C D Ks drive the cycle, and checkpoints stop it when something's wrong. Mitosis makes two identical cells. Meiosis makes four different haploid cells. Non-disjunction gives the wrong chromosome number. Now try the practice questions!
